name: Leukoencephalopathy with Thalamus and Brainstem Anomalies and High Lactate Syndrome
aliases: Leukoencephalopathy with Thalamic and Brainstem Abnormalities and Elevated Lactate

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for LTBL Syndrome

criteria.description: MRI demonstrating leukoencephalopathy with characteristic thalamic and brainstem signal abnormalities
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid indicating mitochondrial dysfunction
Presence of neurological symptoms including developmental delay and hypotonia
Identification of pathogenic variants in the EARS2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: characteristic MRI findings, elevated lactate, and neurological clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetric T2 hyperintensities in thalamus and brainstem on MRI
searchTerms: bright spots in deep brain areas on MRI
symmetrical brainstem and thalamus MRI changes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated lactate concentration in cerebrospinal fluid or blood
searchTerms: high lactic acid in blood or spinal fluid
elevated lactate levels in body fluids
increased lactic acid in cerebrospinal fluid

laboratory: Elevated lactate in blood and cerebrospinal fluid
imaging: MRI showing symmetric leukoencephalopathy with thalamic and brainstem signal abnormalities
Diffusion restriction in affected white matter regions
genetic: Pathogenic variants in EARS2 gene (mitochondrial glutamyl-tRNA synthetase)
other: Abnormal mitochondrial respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Similar MRI findings but caused by DARS2 mutations

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
references: Steenweg ME et al. EARS2 mutations cause a distinctive leukoencephalopathy with thalamus and brainstem involvement and high lactate. Brain. 2012.
Orphanet: Leukoencephalopathy with thalamus and brainstem anomalies and high lactate syndrome. ORPHA314051.
Wang J et al. Clinical and molecular characterization of EARS2-related leukoencephalopathy. Neurology. 2014.
